public_rationale: The evidence documents both important limitations and substantial capabilities. Neither establishes the categorical publication-date conclusion. A Turing-test result is not a comprehensive test of the post's criteria, while earlier reasoning failures do not prove that every plausible candidate lacked AGI. Scoring this claim would require choosing a consequential threshold that Marcus did not supply.
limitations: This is a historical assessment; later model improvements do not contradict the claim.
No claim is made about undisclosed systems.
The evidence does not supply an agreed pass/fail boundary for AGI.

statement.document_title: Rumors of AGI’s arrival have been greatly exaggerated

from_speaker: humanity has already achieved artificial general intelligence
our_interpretation: Read the statement as denying that AGI had been achieved by publication, rather than predicting future failure.
Use the surrounding definition: robust, flexible competence across broad tasks and environments, including adaptation to novelty.
Do not require perfection, consciousness, embodiment, or superhuman performance.
Use a post-date snapshot of systems available on 2026-02-17. Earlier evaluations are context unless they establish the state of those systems at that date.
criteria.support_condition: Adequate evaluations of the plausible AGI candidates available at publication establish substantial failures of the specified broad competence and adaptation requirements.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system available by publication demonstrably satisfies those requirements across credible, sufficiently broad evaluations.
